correctness.rationale: At all a,rho>0, b real, ell>a, beta in [0,1), direct subproblem differentiation yields Phi. Exact stationarity uses H_a with discriminant 4(1-4a). Its fold order proves the complete root count; the Jacobian Schur conditions reduce exactly to F''/D. The exact witness factorizes and has Hessian signs +/−/+, and F(1)>F(4+sqrt(7)) is proved by explicit rational/logarithmic inequalities. All fold degeneracies are stated as unproved for nonlinear stability. Analytic proof plus replayed exact SymPy checker.

originality.rationale: The full 2026 primary algorithm derives critical-point convergence but not its exact two-state linearization or parameter-independent bistable equilibrium type. Known Cauchy proximal cubic and convexity threshold, and older saddle-instability theorems for *different* damped IRL algorithms, are explicitly treated as prior work. The joint all-admissible-parameters dynamical phase diagram plus a strict suboptimal attracting basin is not implied by their statements. Targeted semantic search yielded no equivalent published record; this is a self-review, not a claim of exhaustively proved priority.
residual_risks: The Cauchy stationary cubic and convexity boundary were already known; they are not the novelty of this finding.
A generic earlier inertia/majorization-minimization local stability theorem could conceivably imply the specific Jacobian classification, beyond the literature inspected.
Semantic database searching cannot certify exhaustive novelty or access to unpublished work.

value.rationale: A sharp natural phase classification for a canonical Gaussian-plus-log sparse-recovery model identifies precisely when the actual 2026 inertial reweighting iteration develops two robust stable equilibria, one provably nonoptimal for an exact rational-parameter example. It bears directly on model initialization and the inability of admissible inertia/proximal parameters to remove local-trap structure; it is not merely a log-cubic or table recomputation.
